data.hypothesis: The SSE2 path already classifies starters and continuation requirements across 16-byte blocks, but performs several SIMD comparisons to validate restricted second-byte ranges. Checking those ranges scalarly only for E0, ED, F0, or F4 starter lanes may reduce per-block SIMD work when those starters are infrequent. Lane-15 checks remain deferred across the block boundary, and the existing scalar validator remains the fallback/control. This is an unmeasured hybrid; the official mixed-width n=65536 timing will determine whether it helps.

memory_lessons.applicability: This candidate keeps the whole-block SSE2 classification while changing only exceptional scalar-value range checks; it should be judged independently from ASCII-span scanning.
memory_lessons.claim: The T1 catalog has three distinct programs and no repeats, but its only valid measured child (1bef6299446e4809) was slower than baseline: 57.50 µs versus 49.62 µs. The 8-byte SWAR attempt 0eeba011b99c4165 ended runtime_failed without a timing. SIMD and mask hypotheses therefore remain unproven by these measurements.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this restricted-lane hybrid with the unchanged build and official mixed-width n=65536 case; retain the scalar control and run the official correctness cases.

data.notes: Catalog comparison: T1 source_diversity reports 3 distinct programs and no repeats. The valid ASCII-block hybrid measured 57.50 µs against the 49.62 µs baseline; this experiment changes the full-vector validator rather than repeating that scan. The separate T2 result 31112ea757f04c4a measured 39.98 µs, but is a different algorithm and does not establish a benefit for this SIMD design. Prior T1 SWAR runs 0eeba011b99c4165 and c557b10fc09a4c93 were runtime_failed without timings; h02 and h03 had correctness failures. No speed or correctness result is claimed here. The SSE2 path remains guarded by the existing compile-time macro, with the scalar path retained; no flags, ABI, output, or thread budget were changed.
transformations: Retained the supplied scalar UTF-8 validator and the existing compile-time SSE2/scalar fallback.
Kept 16-byte SIMD starter classification, shifted continuation requirements, carry state, and bounded scalar tail handling.
Replaced vector-wide restricted second-byte range comparisons with conditional scalar checks only for E0, ED, F0, and F4 lanes.
Deferred restricted checks for lane 15 to the next vector while preserving exact second-byte restrictions and the existing ABI/output.
